source.title: On the Demystification of Knowledge Distillation: A Residual Network Perspective
source.authors: Nandan Kumar Jha; Rajat Saini; Sparsh Mittal

record.tranche_reason: The paper compares training accuracy of residual and non-residual CIFAR-100 networks, including results with and without knowledge distillation. It tests whether shortcut removal and KD affect training outcomes, using classification accuracy rather than training error.
record.gate_note: Rows report the paper's own CIFAR-100 test accuracies for residual baselines, non-residual baselines, and distilled non-residual students. These are test-set accuracy results, not training classification error. Tables 1–6 report accuracy drop and distillation gain; the reported values do not establish whether training error stalled above zero. Rows are kept separate by architecture, g/G configuration, and teacher/student setting where the tables provide separate results. Table 7–9 parameter and FLOP values, activation visualizations, and cited prior-work results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study reports CIFAR-100 test accuracy after shortcut removal and knowledge distillation. These outcomes cannot establish V3's training-error degradation or its prevention by shortcuts. It reports no training-error, convergence-speed, initialization-comparison, or stability measurements that test another version. Its optimization explanations are hypotheses rather than independently demonstrated results.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the empirical conclusion: KD can recover or exceed residual-baseline test accuracy in some shallower non-residual configurations, while recovery remains incomplete in deeper networks. The authors additionally propose a Trainee-Mentor interpretation and attribute KD's benefit to better effective initialization and convergence into favorable loss regions; the reported experiments do not directly establish that mechanism.
record.recipe_differences: The study removes residual shortcuts from CIFAR-100 classifiers and trains the resulting non-residual students with hard targets or knowledge distillation from residual teachers. It reports test accuracy rather than training error.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported test accuracy and distillation gains vary across architecture, depth, width, group-convolution setting, and teacher configuration.

fits_no_version.finding: Shortcut removal lowers reported CIFAR-100 test accuracy, especially in deeper WRNs. For g2, residual versus non-residual accuracy is 71.13% versus 64.01% for WRN-22x2, and 71.21% versus 43.92% for WRN-40x2 (Tables 3 and 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Removing residual shortcuts can reduce CIFAR-100 test accuracy, with larger reductions in deeper networks under the tested recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: KD can exceed the residual baseline in some configurations but does not fully restore deeper students' test accuracy. WRN-22x10 NR-G2 reaches 78.17% against a 75.46% residual baseline; WRN-40x2 NR-G2 reaches at most 64.50% against 68.52% (Tables 4 and 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Knowledge distillation can compensate for shortcut removal in test accuracy in some shallower configurations, while recovery remains incomplete in the tested deeper networks.

record.problems: The reported outcome is classification accuracy, not training error, so it cannot answer whether these networks reach near-zero training error. The tables provide no uncertainty estimates. Results are on CIFAR-100 only.
record.rows_left_out: No rows retained: Tables 1–6 report test accuracy and accuracy changes, while the versions concern training error or training dynamics; the paper gives no corresponding training-error outcomes.

untested.parts: Training classification error, including near-zero error with corrupted or random labels and its dependence on model size or training recipe.
Spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and their dependence on excess student width.

Depth-dependent training-error degradation, longer-training controls, its prevention by identity shortcuts, and the initialization exceptions. Test accuracy after shortcut removal does not measure these outcomes.

Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, training speed, and trainable depth. KD is described as providing better initialization, but initialization schemes and these outcomes are not compared.
Learning rates relative to stability thresholds, transient training-loss increases, curvature dynamics, and divergence.
Batch normalization versus no normalization for training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and training with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's V3 status from tested_not_extracted to not_tested. No rows were supplied, and the excluded test-accuracy results are already declared in rows_left_out. Neither the accuracy comparisons nor the selected-class activation visualizations justify verdicts on training-error degradation.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 training error, corrupted or random labels, SGD/Adam comparison, and claims about model size, training duration, smaller models, early stopping, or regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious local minima, and student width relative to teacher width.

The study tests shortcut removal and KD in CIFAR-100 residual networks and reports test accuracy, but no training-error measurements. It does not compare longer training to distinguish a training-error degradation effect.
Initialization comparisons and signal/gradient propagation outcomes.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss rises, curvature or sharpness dynamics, and divergence.
Batch normalization versus no normalization as a training-speed or learning-rate comparison; Fixup recipes.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
